question: A platform team is standardizing how prompt templates are built across several internal applications so that fixed instructions and variable inputs stay cleanly separated. Which of the following statements about prompt templates and variables are accurate? (Select all that apply)
options: A) A prompt template combines fixed content, such as static instructions, with variable content, such as user input or retrieved RAG context, using placeholders for the dynamic parts
B) Separating fixed and variable content improves testability because different input values can be swapped in without rewriting the entire prompt structure
C) Prompt templates require the fixed instruction text to be rewritten from scratch every time the variable input changes, so no structure can be reused across calls
D) Prompt templates are only usable inside claude.ai's chat interface and cannot be used with direct API calls or Console-based workflows
E) Wrapping template variables in XML tags is a documented way to add clearer structure around the dynamic content when it is inserted into the prompt
correct_answers: A) A prompt template combines fixed content, such as static instructions, with variable content, such as user input or retrieved RAG context, using placeholders for the dynamic parts
B) Separating fixed and variable content improves testability because different input values can be swapped in without rewriting the entire prompt structure
E) Wrapping template variables in XML tags is a documented way to add clearer structure around the dynamic content when it is inserted into the prompt
explanations: Correct. A prompt template combines fixed content and variable content (like user input or RAG-retrieved context) using placeholders for the dynamic parts.
Correct. Testability is one of the documented benefits: different inputs and edge cases can be tested by changing only the variable portion.
Incorrect. The entire point of separating fixed and variable content is that the fixed instruction text is reused unchanged across calls, and only the placeholder content changes.
Incorrect. It is the reverse: claude.ai does not currently support prompt templates or variables, while the Claude Console and direct API calls do.
Correct. Wrapping template variables in XML tags is a documented tip for adding clearer structure to prompt templates.
